title: Upstream fidelity and runtime-evidence maintenance
summary: Review ten material upstream changes across reconstruction fidelity, decompilation, ports, networking and original-hardware evidence.
notes: The CPU audit queue contained zero unresolved source/target CPU areas. This pass nevertheless captured newly explicit Xtensa output evidence for ESP32 Locomotive BASIC and the Atari ST port's documented 2 MB runtime floor; it did not infer a minimum from a platform or language. Primary commits were reviewed, and no upstream project was compiled or executed by the tracker.

source_updates.reason: Reviewed the new save-layout, blitter-contract and viewport-provenance evidence across the six DOS images; retained the explicit reachability and whole-game limits.
Reviewed the two progress commits and their updated README counters, per-function development/holdout evidence and explicitly thin coverage limits.
Reviewed the authentic Nexus BKR Continue replay and FM Towns startup trace work; preserved the distinction between retail-reference capture and Firestaff implementation.
Reviewed the shared LevelState, render, pause, particle, puzzle and memory-card typing refactors; no separate nested project appeared.
Reviewed the exact three-profile Xtensa build evidence and the independent original-CPC scalar STRING oracle package; no second project root appeared.
Reviewed the kernel socket-manager, packetless W5100 TX/RX, Telnet and first WGET integration; no separate utility project was promoted.
Reviewed the Atari ST music extraction and Amiga-to-ST conversion series; the port remains part of Ambermoon rather than a newly titled project.
Reviewed the English Amiga data, map-music, sample, outro graphics and COSO/TFMX playback additions; all remain within the existing Amber framework project.
Reviewed the disaster, multi-platform minimap and Aquarius+ text-layer work; the ports remain one shared reconstruction project.
Reviewed the pinned NetX Duo FIN, recovery-boundary and DATA/FIN SACK updates; the vendor submodule remains part of AmiNetXDuo.

build.narrative: The reviewed pass 21, 25 and 26 reports account for the fixed 55,015-byte Win16 save slot, exercise signed page-gate and split-boundary caller contracts in 4,536 cases, and verify 492 default viewport setter-to-blitter chains across six DOS images.
build.limitations: The caller-contract run intercepts the original blitter, the viewport run mocks two downstream dependencies, and neither establishes full DOS/VGA reachability, save/load parity or playable-game fidelity.
build.next_action: Connect the bounded save, viewport and blitter findings to original runtime execution, framebuffer output and end-to-end save/load checks.

project.status: AmiNetXDuo now pins reviewed NetX Duo TCP corrections for FIN acknowledgement, recovery boundaries/timers and DATA/FIN SACK recovery; the existing physical A3000/A2065 profile remains the only measured tracker runtime profile.

identity.narrative: Independent bsdsocket.library implementation for classic AmigaOS backed by hosted ThreadX/NetX Duo, SANA-II network drivers and command-line networking clients.

Current1.0.0-rc1; Pi Wi-Fi driver experimental and hardware coverage varies. MIT main stack and ThreadX/NetX; exceptions include BSD-2 NE2000 code, Dropbear MIT-style, separate Commodore/Sylvan Installer notices, MPL2 CA roots/WiFiPi and BSD WirelessManager. README licence table pins their scopes.

build.next_action: Retain the physical A3000/A2065 profile and seek end-to-end recovery evidence before broadening runtime or interoperability claims.
